title: Check each requirement's format, as strict validation does

expected.says: Run's report for the tiny portfolio matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def check_requirement(req: Requirement, where: str) -> list[Issue]
blueprint.contract: The issues of one requirement, each an Issue(level, where, message) with the `where` it is given, in this order: an ERROR 'requirement "<name>" has no text under its header' when req.text is empty, or else a WARNING 'requirement "<name>" should contain SHALL or MUST in its text' when the text has neither as a whole upper-case word (KEYWORD); an ERROR 'requirement "<name>" must include at least one scenario' when no scenario in req.scenarios has a non-empty body; then, for each scenario with a body, a WARNING 'scenario "<name>" is missing <what>' when has_steps finds no WHEN or GIVEN step ('a WHEN or GIVEN step') or no THEN step ('a THEN step'), both joined by ' and ' when both are missing. An empty list when the requirement keeps every rule.
blueprint.idea: A requirement states one behaviour with SHALL or MUST in its text, not only its header; a scenario counts only with steps under it, and needs a trigger and an outcome. Strict validation fails on warnings too.

blueprint.contract: As before, then one more line about the project's living specs: 'openspec: <n> specs, <r> requirements, <s> scenarios; strict validation passed' (or FAILED), counting openspec/specs/*/spec.md next to main.py, their requirements and scenarios, and passing when specs_check.validate's issues pass in strict mode for every item.
blueprint.idea: The project checks its own specs on every run, as `openspec validate --strict` would.

cases: a requirement with no text under its header is an error
text without SHALL or MUST is a warning
a SHALL in the requirement's header alone does not count
a requirement with no scenario is an error
a scenario heading with nothing under it does not count
a scenario without a THEN step is a warning
strict mode fails on a warning that plain mode passes
this project's own specs pass strict validation
